pinyin: zhòng shǎng zhī xià, bì yǒu yǒng fū
literal: heavy · reward · under · must · have · brave · man
natural: where there is a big reward, brave men appear

meaning.en: A generous reward will always motivate people to take risks.
meaning.zh: 给予丰厚的奖赏，就会有人不怕危险去做。

equivalents: a big prize finds willing volunteers

examples.zh: 重赏之下，必有勇夫，奖金一出，报名的人就多了。
examples.en: A big reward brings out the brave; once the bonus was announced, many signed up.

examples.zh: 悬赏十万，果然重赏之下，必有勇夫。
examples.en: With a 100,000 yuan bounty, sure enough, someone stepped up.

usage.en: Neutral to slightly cynical about incentives.
usage.zh: 中性，略带对利益驱动的调侃。

story.en: The Three Strategies, attributed to Huang Shigong, quotes an old military text: 'under fragrant bait there must be fish; under heavy rewards there must be brave men' (香饵之下，必有死鱼；重赏之下，必有勇夫).
story.zh: 《黄石公三略·上略》引军谶：“香饵之下，必有死鱼；重赏之下，必有勇夫。”

date.en: Han dynasty, c. 1st c. BC–2nd c. AD

meaning.en: To eat one's fill all day without doing anything useful.
meaning.zh: 整天吃饱了饭，什么正事也不干。

examples.zh: 他饱食终日，无所事事。
examples.en: He idles about all day doing nothing.

examples.zh: 年轻人不能饱食终日，要找点正事做。
examples.en: Young people shouldn't just idle away; find something worthwhile to do.

story.en: Confucius: 'Those who eat their fill all day and use their minds on nothing — how hard it is for them!' (饱食终日，无所用心，难矣哉).
story.zh: 孔子说：“饱食终日，无所用心，难矣哉！”

usage.en: Criticises idleness. Often 饱食终日，无所用心.
usage.zh: 批评懒散，常说“饱食终日，无所用心”。

meaning.en: Said to return a compliment: 'the same to you'; also, 'we are both just as good (or bad)'.
meaning.zh: 客套话，表示双方都一样；回应对方的夸奖时说自己也差不多。

equivalents: we're as bad as each other

examples.zh: “你的字真漂亮！”“彼此彼此。”
examples.en: 'Your handwriting is lovely!' 'Likewise.'

examples.zh: 他说我偷懒，其实我们彼此彼此。
examples.en: He says I'm lazy, but really we're as bad as each other.

usage.en: Casual response to compliments or in mild teasing. Normally spoken, repeated twice.
usage.zh: 口语中回应夸奖或互相调侃，叠用。

natural: wag the tail to beg for pity

meaning.en: To grovel and fawn in order to win favour.
meaning.zh: 狗摇尾巴乞求怜爱，比喻卑躬屈膝地讨好别人。

equivalents: wag one's tail to beg for favour

examples.zh: 他为了升职，对上司摇尾乞怜。
examples.en: To get promoted, he fawns before his boss.

examples.zh: 他宁死也不向敌人摇尾乞怜。
examples.en: He would rather die than grovel to the enemy.

story.en: Han Yu wrote that if he must wag his tail and beg for pity, it is not his wish (若俛首贴耳，摇尾而乞怜者，非我之志也).
story.zh: 韩愈《应科目时与人书》：“若俛首贴耳，摇尾而乞怜者，非我之志也。”

usage.en: Strongly derogatory, about servility.
usage.zh: 贬义，指奴颜婢膝。

meaning.en: The enemy has far greater numbers than us.
meaning.zh: 敌方人数多，我方人数少，力量悬殊。

examples.zh: 敌众我寡，只能智取，不能硬拼。
examples.en: We are heavily outnumbered, so it must be cunning, not brute force.

examples.zh: 尽管敌众我寡，他们仍坚持到了最后。
examples.en: Though outnumbered, they held out to the end.

usage.en: Often used of battles, sport or negotiations.
usage.zh: 常用于战争、比赛、谈判。

natural: widely informed with a strong memory

meaning.en: Widely read and learned, with an excellent memory.
meaning.zh: 见闻广博，记忆力强。

equivalents: widely read with a great memory

examples.zh: 他博闻强记，几乎没有他不知道的事。
examples.en: He is widely read with a prodigious memory; there is little he doesn't know.

examples.zh: 这位博闻强记的老教授让学生们十分敬佩。
examples.en: The erudite old professor is admired by his students.

usage.en: Praises scholars. Both 强记 and 强识 are used.
usage.zh: 赞扬学者。“强记”“强识”都可以。

natural: failing to decide when one should

meaning.en: Hesitating to make a decision at the moment it is needed.
meaning.zh: 该决断的时候不决断，犹豫不决。

equivalents: dither when decisive action is needed

examples.zh: 当断不断，反受其乱，他错过了最佳时机。
examples.en: Hesitating when he should have decided, he suffered for it and missed the best moment.

examples.zh: 面对危机，领导不能当断不断。
examples.en: In a crisis a leader cannot dither.

story.en: Zhu Ying advised Lord Chunshen: 'When one should decide and does not, one suffers the consequences' (当断不断，反受其乱).
story.zh: 朱英劝春申君：“当断不断，反受其乱。”

usage.en: Usually the full warning 当断不断，反受其乱 (whoever hesitates is lost).
usage.zh: 常说“当断不断，反受其乱”。

meaning.en: A person who shows misplaced kindness to the wicked and gets hurt for it.
meaning.zh: 对恶人讲仁慈、结果害了自己的糊涂好人。

examples.zh: 对骗子心软，你就是现代的东郭先生。
examples.en: Being soft on a swindler, you are a modern Mr Dongguo.

examples.zh: 别做东郭先生，对坏人不能心慈手软。
examples.en: Don't be a Mr Dongguo; you can't show mercy to the wicked.

story.en: In the tale, scholar Dongguo hides a hunted wolf in his bag; once the hunters leave, the wolf tries to eat him.
story.zh: 东郭先生救了被猎人追赶的中山狼，狼脱险后却想吃他。

usage.en: A person-type idiom from the fable of the wolf of Zhongshan (中山狼); usually with 做 or 像.
usage.zh: 出自“中山狼”寓言，多说“做东郭先生”。

natural: a general of a defeated army

meaning.en: A person who has failed or been defeated, often one who is humbled and unfit to boast.
meaning.zh: 打了败仗的将领，泛指失败者。

examples.zh: 败军之将，不敢言勇。
examples.en: A defeated general dare not speak of valour.

examples.zh: 败军之将不可言勇，他选择沉默。
examples.en: A beaten general should not boast of courage, so he stayed silent.

story.en: Han Xin asked the captured Zhao strategist Li Zuoche for advice; Li replied: 'A defeated general may not speak of bravery' (败军之将，不可以言勇).
story.zh: 李左车对韩信说：“臣闻败军之将，不可以言勇。”

usage.en: Mostly in the saying 败军之将，不敢言勇, as self-effacing or sneering.
usage.zh: 多见于“败军之将，不敢言勇”，用于自谦或讥讽。

meaning.en: A polite way of saying 'I have a favour to ask', admitting it may be an imposition.
meaning.zh: 请求别人帮忙时的客气话，表示请求可能不合情理。

equivalents: I hope you won't mind my asking

examples.zh: 我有一个不情之请，想借你的车用一天。
examples.en: I have a favour to ask: may I borrow your car for a day?

examples.zh: 冒昧提出这个不情之请，还望见谅。
examples.en: Forgive me for making this imposing request.

usage.en: Humble formula, used for oneself only. Never describe other people's requests this way.
usage.zh: 谦辞，只用于自己的请求，不能用于别人。

meaning.en: To kill people in huge numbers; extremely brutal.
meaning.zh: 杀的人像乱麻一样多，形容极其凶残。

examples.zh: 这个军阀杀人如麻，百姓闻风丧胆。
examples.en: The warlord killed without limit, and the people trembled at his name.

examples.zh: 小说里的杀手个个杀人如麻。
examples.en: The killers in the novel are all ruthless murderers.

usage.en: Strongly negative, often used of tyrants or villains.
usage.zh: 贬义很重，多指暴君、恶人。

meaning.en: Fierce and brutal like wolves and tigers; also, extremely strong appetite (colloquially).
meaning.zh: 像狼和虎一样凶狠残暴；口语也形容极其有力或食欲旺盛。

examples.zh: 如狼似虎的恶霸闯进了村子。
examples.en: The savage thugs burst into the village.

examples.zh: 孩子们饿了一天，吃饭时如狼似虎。
examples.en: The children, hungry all day, wolfed their food down like wolves.

usage.en: Mostly about violent people; also used for ravenous eating.
usage.zh: 多形容凶狠的人，也可形容吃相凶猛。

natural: may Heaven and Earth destroy me

meaning.en: A solemn oath: may Heaven and Earth destroy me; also, utterly unforgivable.
meaning.zh: 发誓的话，意思是天地都不容；也指罪恶极大。

examples.zh: 我要是骗你，天诛地灭！
examples.en: If I'm lying to you, may heaven strike me down!

examples.zh: 这种伤天害理的人，天诛地灭。
examples.en: A person who does such wicked things will be punished by Heaven and Earth.

usage.en: Mostly in oaths. Strong; best kept for emphatic or dramatic speech.
usage.zh: 多用于发誓，语气重，用于强调或戏剧场景。

meaning.en: To cheer and jump for joy.
meaning.zh: 高兴得大声欢呼、跳跃。

examples.zh: 听到获奖的消息，同学们欢呼雀跃。
examples.en: Hearing of the award, the pupils cheered and jumped for joy.

examples.zh: 孩子们见到雪，欢呼雀跃。
examples.en: The children cheered with delight at the snow.

usage.en: Joyful and lively, typically about groups. 雀 is read què here.
usage.zh: 多形容群体兴奋。“雀”读què。

meaning.en: What one says is reasonable and holds together logically.
meaning.zh: 说的话有道理，讲得通。

examples.zh: 他的解释言之成理，大家都点了头。
examples.en: His explanation made sense and everyone nodded.

examples.zh: 这个观点言之成理，值得讨论。
examples.en: The view is plausible and worth discussing.

story.en: Xunzi says of some schools that 'their views have grounds and their words make sense' (持之有故，言之成理).
story.zh: 《荀子·非十二子》：“然而其持之有故，其言之成理。”

usage.en: Often paired with 持之有故. Slightly cautious praise: it is reasonable, not necessarily true.
usage.zh: 常与“持之有故”连用，是肯定，但不一定表示正确。

meaning.en: Even thieves have their own code of conduct; used of the honour among wrongdoers.
meaning.zh: 强盗也有自己的行为准则；比喻坏人中也有讲规矩的。

examples.zh: 盗亦有道，他从不抢穷人的东西。
examples.en: There is honour among thieves; he never robs the poor.

examples.zh: 盗亦有道，这个骗子也有自己的底线。
examples.en: Even this swindler has a line he won't cross.

story.en: In Zhuangzi, the thief Zhi says thieves also have 'sageliness, courage, righteousness, wisdom and benevolence' (盗亦有道).
story.zh: 《庄子·胠箧》中盗跖说盗贼也有“圣、勇、义、智、仁”之道。

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Often quoted when even a bad person shows principles. Not a compliment on crime itself.
usage.zh: 常用来说明坏人也有底线，并非赞美犯罪。

literal: mountain goblins · water goblins · evil spirits

meaning.en: Evil spirits and monsters; figuratively all kinds of villains and wicked people.
meaning.zh: 传说中山林里的各种妖怪；比喻各种坏人。

examples.zh: 光明之下，魑魅魍魉无处藏身。
examples.en: In the light, demons and villains have nowhere to hide.

examples.zh: 神话中的魑魅魍魉出没于深山。
examples.en: In myth, goblins and monsters haunt the deep mountains.

story.en: The Zuozhuan notes that Yu's bronze cauldrons showed spirits so people could avoid 'goblins and demons' (魑魅魍魉).
story.zh: 《左传·宣公三年》：“故民入川泽山林，不逢不若，螭魅罔两，莫能逢之。”

usage.en: Literary and dramatic. Rarely used of ordinary people.
usage.zh: 文学色彩浓，不用于一般人。

literal: literati · each other · look down on

meaning.en: Writers and scholars tend to look down on one another.
meaning.zh: 文人之间互相轻视，各自认为自己高明。

examples.zh: 自古文人相轻，学界的争论从未停止。
examples.en: Scholars have always belittled one another, and academic disputes never end.

examples.zh: 别让文人相轻的习气影响合作。
examples.en: Don't let scholars' rivalry spoil cooperation.

story.en: Cao Pi wrote: 'Literati look down on one another, and it has always been so' (文人相轻，自古而然).
story.zh: 曹丕《典论·论文》：“文人相轻，自古而然。”

usage.en: Mostly negative; often in 文人相轻，自古而然.
usage.zh: 贬义，常说“文人相轻，自古而然”。

meaning.en: Obstinate and slow-witted, impossible to teach.
meaning.zh: 愚昧顽固，不明事理。

examples.zh: 对这种冥顽不灵的人，说再多也没用。
examples.en: It is pointless to say more to someone so hopelessly stubborn.

examples.zh: 他冥顽不灵，始终不肯认错。
examples.en: He is obstinate and never admits his mistake.

story.en: In his 'Address to the Crocodiles', Han Yu scolds any crocodile that stays on 'dull, stubborn and unresponsive' (冥顽不灵) and ignores his warning.
story.zh: 韩愈《祭鳄鱼文》斥责鳄鱼若“冥顽不灵”，不听警告，必将受罚。

usage.en: Derogatory, used of people who refuse to learn or change.
usage.zh: 贬义，指不肯接受道理的人。

synonyms: 茅坑里的石头——又臭又硬

meaning.en: To persist in wrongdoing and refuse to repent.
meaning.zh: 坚持作恶，不肯悔改。

examples.zh: 对怙恶不悛的惯犯要依法严惩。
examples.en: Persistent, unrepentant offenders must be severely punished.

examples.zh: 他屡教不改，怙恶不悛。
examples.en: He ignores every warning and never repents.

usage.en: Formal, legal tone. 悛 is read quān.
usage.zh: 书面、法律语体。“悛”读quān。

natural: cry to heaven and strike the ground

meaning.en: To wail in grief and despair.
meaning.zh: 大声哭喊，捶胸顿足，形容极度悲痛。

examples.zh: 听到噩耗，她呼天抢地，哭倒在地。
examples.en: On hearing the terrible news she wailed and collapsed in tears.

examples.zh: 灾后现场，一片呼天抢地的哭声。
examples.en: At the disaster site, cries of anguish rose everywhere.

usage.en: Extreme grief, sometimes exaggerated. 抢 is read qiāng (to knock).
usage.zh: 形容极度悲痛。“抢”读qiāng。

meaning.en: Gossip and public opinion can be terrifying and do real damage.
meaning.zh: 别人的议论、流言蜚语很可怕。

equivalents: people's tongues are to be feared

examples.zh: 人言可畏，网络暴力能毁掉一个人。
examples.en: Gossip is fearsome; online abuse can ruin someone.

examples.zh: 她因为人言可畏，不敢再去上班。
examples.en: Fearing gossip, she no longer dared to go to work.

story.en: The Book of Songs: 'People's many words are also to be feared' (人之多言，亦可畏也).
story.zh: 《诗经·将仲子》：“人之多言，亦可畏也。”

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Often warning about rumours and cyberbullying.
usage.zh: 常用于警示流言蜚语和网络暴力。
